A quick reminder of the core: regular verbs form the past simple with -ed, as in played, visited and watched.
The nuance is spelling. A verb ending in a consonant + y changes y to -ied (study, studied), but a vowel + y just adds -ed (play, played). A short verb ending consonant-vowel-consonant, stressed at the end, doubles the last consonant (stop, stopped; plan, planned). A verb ending in -e only adds -d (arrive, arrived).
